metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

return.narrative:
当前未检索到补充音乐知识，以下内容仅基于音乐目录事实。
《Where Is My Mind?》在这条世界线里是一个很好的起点：它由 Pixies 演绎，收录于《Surfer Rosa (Remastered)》，时长约 234973 毫秒 [music-api:song:4236643]。这些目录事实本身已经勾勒出一条清晰的路径——从歌曲回到乐队，再从乐队回到专辑，三者构成一个可以逐层展开的小型结构 [music-api:song:4236643]。

沿着乐队这条边继续走，会看到 Pixies 名下还有多首作品，例如《Where Is My Mind》《Here Comes Your Man》《The Thing》《The Happening》《Greens and Blues》《Hey》和《All I Think About Now》 [music-api:artist:98542]。它们与《Where Is My Mind?》共享同一个演绎者，因此适合作为同一世界线内的横向对照：听同一支乐队在不同曲目中的处理方式，比孤立地听一首歌更能显出这条线的形状 [music-api:artist:98542]。

图中还有一条跨向外部场景的边：Pixies 被标注为对 Nirvana 产生了影响 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。这条关系之所以值得继续探索，是因为它把一首歌的局部世界线接入了更大的另类摇滚脉络——资料提到，Pixies 对 Nirvana 有深远影响，并且在美国打入 Billboard 前 60 名之前，就已经在英国拥有三张前十专辑 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。顺着这条边，可以从单曲走向乐队之间的影响关系，而不是停留在曲目清单上。

从 Nirvana 再往外，图连接到一个场景节点：Nirvana 从“Grunge-rock”场景中走出，该场景是西海岸的朋克变体，起源于西雅图，靠近乐队家乡阿伯丁，时间在 1980 年代末 [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。这条边解释了为什么这条世界线不只是一支乐队加一首歌：它把歌曲、乐队、受影响的乐队和场景串成一条可追踪的路径，每一跳都有明确的证据支撑 [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。

需要说明的是，当前知识库只覆盖目录事实与上述影响、场景关系，并没有提供《Where Is My Mind?》的创作背景、发行年份或制作细节，因此这些内容不应被当作已核实的事实来陈述 [music-api:song:4236643]。可继续探索的方向是：在 Pixies 的作品集合内做横向比较，或沿着“Pixies → Nirvana → Grunge-rock 场景”这条影响链向外扩展 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。

sources.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

把视角从单曲拉远到 Pixies 这位艺人，会发现这张图里挂着一串同样值得点开的作品：《Where Is My Mind?》《Where Is My Mind》《The Thing》《The Happening》《Greens and Blues》《Hey》《All I Think About Now》，它们都以 performed_by 的关系指向 Pixies [music-api:artist:98542]。这意味着《Here Comes Your Man》并不是孤立的节点，而是 Pixies 作品网络中的一个入口；沿着这些边继续走，你能在同一艺人的语境下比较不同歌曲，而不是只停留在单曲页面 [music-api:artist:98542]。

这条世界线还向外延伸出一条跨艺人的关系：Pixies 与 Nirvana 之间存在 influenced 关系，而 Nirvana 又通过 emerged_from_scene 连接到 Grunge-rock scene [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。资料中提到，Nirvana 受到包括 Pixies 在内的乐队影响，并且 Nirvana 是从“Grunge-rock”场景中走出来的，该场景是朋克在西海岸的变体，起源于西雅图 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。另有资料指出，Pixies 对 Nirvana 有深远影响，并且在英国曾有三张进入前十的专辑，早于他们进入 Billboard 前 60 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。这些关系解释了为什么从《Here Comes Your Man》出发，可以一路走到 Nirvana 与 Grunge-rock scene 这两个节点 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

metadata.evidence_span:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

evidence_history.title: Assessing an American pop icon
evidence_history.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

evidence_history.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
evidence_history.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

evidence_history.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
evidence_history.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

把视角从单曲拉远到 Pixies 这位艺人，会发现这张图里挂着一串同样值得点开的作品：《Where Is My Mind?》《Where Is My Mind》《The Thing》《The Happening》《Greens and Blues》《Hey》《All I Think About Now》，它们都以 performed_by 的关系指向 Pixies [music-api:artist:98542]。这意味着《Here Comes Your Man》并不是孤立的节点，而是 Pixies 作品网络中的一个入口；沿着这些边继续走，你能在同一艺人的语境下比较不同歌曲，而不是只停留在单曲页面 [music-api:artist:98542]。

这条世界线还向外延伸出一条跨艺人的关系：Pixies 与 Nirvana 之间存在 influenced 关系，而 Nirvana 又通过 emerged_from_scene 连接到 Grunge-rock scene [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。资料中提到，Nirvana 受到包括 Pixies 在内的乐队影响，并且 Nirvana 是从“Grunge-rock”场景中走出来的，该场景是朋克在西海岸的变体，起源于西雅图 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。另有资料指出，Pixies 对 Nirvana 有深远影响，并且在英国曾有三张进入前十的专辑，早于他们进入 Billboard 前 60 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。这些关系解释了为什么从《Here Comes Your Man》出发，可以一路走到 Nirvana 与 Grunge-rock scene 这两个节点 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。

sources.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.evidence_span:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

当前未检索到补充音乐知识，以下内容仅基于音乐目录事实。
《Here Comes Your Man》在这条世界线里是一个很好的起点：它由 Pixies 演唱，收录在同名专辑《Here Comes Your Man》中，时长约 201186 毫秒 [music-api:song:18319295]。这些目录事实本身已经勾勒出一条清晰的路径——从歌曲到艺人，再到专辑，三者互相印证，让你可以顺着任意一个方向继续展开 [music-api:song:18319295]。

把视角从单曲拉远到 Pixies 这位艺人，会发现这张图里挂着一串同样值得点开的作品：《Where Is My Mind?》《Where Is My Mind》《The Thing》《The Happening》《Greens and Blues》《Hey》《All I Think About Now》，它们都以 performed_by 的关系指向 Pixies [music-api:artist:98542]。这意味着《Here Comes Your Man》并不是孤立的节点，而是 Pixies 作品网络中的一个入口；沿着这些边继续走，你能在同一艺人的语境下比较不同歌曲，而不是只停留在单曲页面 [music-api:artist:98542]。

专辑方向同样有可探索的分支。《Where Is My Mind?》归属于《Surfer Rosa (Remastered)》，而《Here Comes Your Man》归属于同名专辑《Here Comes Your Man》 [music-api:song:4236643] [music-api:song:18319295]。两条 belongs_to_album 边把歌曲和专辑连成两组，让你可以在专辑层面观察 Pixies 的曲目组织方式，而不必依赖任何外部叙述 [music-api:song:4236643] [music-api:song:18319295]。

这条世界线还向外延伸出一条跨艺人的关系：Pixies 与 Nirvana 之间存在 influenced 关系，而 Nirvana 又通过 emerged_from_scene 连接到 Grunge-rock scene [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。资料中提到，Nirvana 受到包括 Pixies 在内的乐队影响，并且 Nirvana 是从“Grunge-rock”场景中走出来的，该场景是朋克在西海岸的变体，起源于西雅图 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。另有资料指出，Pixies 对 Nirvana 有深远影响，并且在英国曾有三张进入前十的专辑，早于他们进入 Billboard 前 60 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。这些关系解释了为什么从《Here Comes Your Man》出发，可以一路走到 Nirvana 与 Grunge-rock scene 这两个节点 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。

需要说明的是，当前知识库只覆盖了上述目录事实与有限的场景、影响关系，并没有提供《Here Comes Your Man》这首歌本身的创作背景、发行年份或制作信息，因此这条世界线目前能确认的是“谁演唱、属于哪张专辑、时长多少”，以及 Pixies 在图中与 Nirvana、Grunge-rock scene 的关联 [music-api:song:18319295] [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。继续探索时，建议优先沿着 performed_by 和 belongs_to_album 这两类边展开，因为它们有明确的目录证据支撑；跨艺人的 influenced 与 emerged_from_scene 边则提供了把单曲放进更大场景的线索，但不应被当作对歌曲本身的额外事实 [music-api:song:18319295] [music-api:artist:98542] [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d] [knowledge:scene:891610c9c8887e424a61c90b]。

sources.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.
